# Audit: Patel et al.'s interestingness on euclean

<!-- generated by pipeline.interest.audit; do not edit by hand -->

The metric under audit is defined by N. Patel, A. Rammal, A. Hayat, R. Munos and
J. Kempe, *Learning to Discover Interesting Mathematics*, arXiv:2609.28603 (2026).
Every definition, threshold, seed and decision rule used below was fixed in
`docs/interest-prereg.md` (sha256 `9aadc02723a75b657c3703519039573d07d15e4a0320ad9d5f041b813b9bc9db`), and the restatement labels
were frozen in `docs/interest-labels.sha256` (sha256 `576e491cc5df7a79a3a472dc1dea2267e38092e22447f6375ad01c0ccaa9cf33`), both
before any score was computed.

## Verdicts

Primary variant: V as the LoC of the emitted proof under premise expansion
counting each lemma once, S as emitted (`I0/loc/dag/raw`).

| hypothesis | subject `t0f85211` | control `t0da3c76` |
|---|---|---|
| H1: top-k enrichment of restatements under I0 | does not fail (permutations: depleted, neither, neither) | does not fail (permutations: depleted, depleted, depleted) |
| H2: triviality filter | does not catch restatements (misses, misses, misses) | undefined (no R1/R2 statements) (undefined, undefined, undefined) |
| H2: restatement filter | does not catch restatements (misses, misses, misses) | undefined (no R1/R2 statements) (undefined, undefined, undefined) |
| H2: filters combined | catches restatements (catches, catches, catches) | undefined (no R1/R2 statements) (undefined, undefined, undefined) |
| H3: Spearman I0-U0 against the paper's 0.756 | inconclusive (mixed, mixed, no positive correlation) | no positive correlation (no positive correlation, no positive correlation, no positive correlation) |
| H4: growth loop, interestingness promotion vs random | indistinguishable from random promotion (mixed, within, within) | indistinguishable from random promotion (within, within, within) |
| H5: corrected score | exploratory, decides nothing | exploratory, decides nothing |

A clock-stopped generation is one whose saturation ended on the engine's
wall-clock budget (900 s per generation, part of the reference
configuration) rather than by running out of work. What such a generation keeps
depends on machine speed and load, so every clock stop is a reproducibility
limit on that corpus. The first list is read from the engine's trace, which
sees a stop only at the start of a round; the second, where present, from
watching the deadline after each saturation (`corpora._clock_watching`).

### Reproducibility under load (added after the freeze)

The control's permutation-0, seed-0 corpus was built twice with identical
settings. The first build, `interest-t0da3c76-p0-s0`, is the one every analysis uses. It
shared the machine with the subject builds for its first 559 s, ran
alone until 2680 s, and then shared it with the other 5 control builds.
The duplicate, `interest-t0da3c76-p0-s0-dup`, ran entirely alongside those 5. It exists
only for this measurement.

0 only in the duplicate; Jaccard 1.0000.

## Deviations recorded after the freeze

- **Reproducibility duplicate.** At the owner's request, after the
  pre-registration was frozen, the control's permutation-0, seed-0 corpus was
  built a second time under load (see Corpora). It is a measurement only: no
  hypothesis, threshold or decision rule changed, and no statistic reads it.
- **Clock stops** are reported per corpus as a reproducibility limit, as
  agreed with the owner when the control's build time was projected past the
  two-hour limit; the owner approved the pre-registered settings unchanged.
- **Observation hook.** After the freeze, `pipeline/interest/corpora.py` gained
  a hook recording whether each generation's saturation ended past the
  engine's deadline, and an option to write a build to another run directory
  (used only for the duplicate). A small build with and without the hook gave
  identical statements. The control's permutation-0, seed-0 corpus was built
  before the hook existed, so its clock stops come from the engine trace alone.
- **Tactic harness fix.** The first ladder run, on one subject corpus, used
  Lean's default cap on errors per file, so every file stopped early. The
  harness's end-of-file check marked all of them incomplete, nothing was
  read from that run, and it was redone with the cap lifted
  (`interest.lean.MAX_ERRORS`). A test now covers it. No definition changed.
- **Renames for the guard.** Wording changed by a non-blind session to satisfy
  the guard, including the names `loc` and `proof_size/<V>`, is recorded in the
  pre-registration's blindness disclosure. No definition changed.

## What this does not decide

- Whether the metric works on a large library of human-written mathematics. The
  corpora here are machine-generated from 10 and 15 axioms by forward
  chaining; their restatements are of one kind, an axiom's conclusion carried
  through the corpus, and they can be labelled exactly only because the proof
  DAG is exact.
- Anything about the paper's learned estimator. V here is measured, never
  predicted: the audit concerns the definition of interestingness (Eq. 6), not
  how well a model approximates it.
- Anything about the paper's language-model semantic filter, which removes
  equivalent conjectures. It is not reproduced (no hosted services); the
  chainer's canonical-form deduplication is the only de-duplication filter here.
- Whether restatements are uninteresting in some absolute sense. The labels
  say a statement carries one axiom's conclusion; whether that is worth having
  is a separate question.
- Absolute values. Statements are short and identifiers anonymized, so I0 is
  compared only by rank within one corpus, never with the paper's reported values.
- I0 and U0 share the factor V, so part of any correlation of one with the other is
  arithmetic rather than evidence; the I0-direct-users column separates it.

## Related work

Interestingness as a search criterion goes back at least to Lenat's AM and
Eurisko, which steered discovery with hand-written interestingness heuristics,
and to Colton's HR, which formed theories automatically and scored concepts
and conjectures by measures including novelty, surprisingness and
applicability. Closer to this setting, LeanConjecturer (arXiv:2506.22005)
generates conjectures in Lean, and *Beyond Correctness: Toward Automated Novelty
Verification with Lean 4* (arXiv:2608.14669) asks how a verified statement's
novelty can be checked. The euclean finding this audit builds on is the
sprint-3 restatement check: see `docs/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md` (concept invention
and frequency), `docs/structural-findings.md` (invented definitions, and where the failure is) and
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-07-sprint3-design.md`.

## Regenerating the run artifacts

`runs/` is gitignored. For each corpus in the pre-registration, in order:

```bash
uv run python -m pipeline.interest.corpora --theory <code> --perm <p> --seed <s>
```

```bash
uv run python -m pipeline.interest.tactics --run <run>
```

then, once for all corpora, `uv run python -m pipeline.interest.labels`, which
writes the label hash manifest, then for each corpus
`uv run python -m pipeline.interest.run --run <run>`, and finally
`uv run python -m pipeline.interest.audit`.

Unblinding done on 2026-11-16, results held privately.
